svg.title: Fig. 17 — The diacaustic for μ > 1: the evolute of a hyperbola
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 17, page 19. Section: caustics.

g.data-text: The source S in the rare medium (right) and S̄, its reflection in the line L, which here separates a rare medium (right) from a dense one (left). The index μ = ½SS̄ / (semi-transverse axis) > 1 fixes the hyperbola.
Points of the hyperbola with foci S, S̄: for a chosen length r, the arcs of radius r about S̄ and of radius r − SS̄/μ about S meet at P, with PS̄ − PS = SS̄/μ. Repeat for several r.
The hyperbola with foci S, S̄, real axis SS̄/μ and eccentricity μ: the locus of the point P of Fig. 15.
Draw the normals of the hyperbola, the lines PQT, which are the refracted rays: each bisects the angle SPS̄. Each normal touches the caustic.
The caustic is the envelope of these normals: the evolute of the hyperbola. Each branch has a cusp on the axis SS̄ (beyond the foci) and runs off to infinity in two arms.
